what: The district has edited its School Committee page since we crawled it. 158,625 bytes in the bucket against 158,675 on disk.
how_found: the same read-back check during the archive push
evidence: a 50-byte difference on a page we fetched once; the bucket copy is the earlier crawl and the lock keeps it, which is the archive working rather than failing

what: THE PUBLISHED PAGE IS NOT BYTE-REPRODUCIBLE, so a re-fetch of one of these HTML files will never match the sha256 the catalogue holds and that is not the district changing anything. Google stamps a fresh `nonce` into every `pubhtml` response, and the district’s Google Sites landing page comes back a different length on consecutive requests. The CSV exports beside them ARE stable byte for byte, which is why the extractor reads those and why change detection compares those. Recorded here so a link or copy check reporting these as drifted is read as what it is rather than as the town editing a page.
how_found: two fetches of the same three addresses, seconds apart, compared
evidence: the district page 118,262 bytes then 118,164; the high school pubhtml 53,194 both times and different bytes; the high school CSV 5,244 bytes and identical

what: The copy on disk is not the copy the manifest recorded, and neither is the copy in the bucket. This key is a LEGACY export: until 26 September 2026 `fetch_dls_property.py` wrote every re-fetch to this one fixed filename, so each run overwrote the file, the manifest re-hashed from disk and followed it, and the bucket -- which a ten-year lock forbids overwriting -- kept whichever version reached it first. Three values for one key, and none of them is wrong: they are three fetches of a report DLS regenerates on its own gateway. The naming rule that replaced this on 26 September puts a date and a content hash in every export name, so no key is ever written twice and this cannot recur. The current copy is state-dls/assessedvalues-2026-09-26-272171893ca3.xlsx, archived under its own key.
how_found: measured: sync_archive.py --manifest refused, naming manifest 65caf52de3b0… against disk a15a81c7d1ac…. It had refused every run since 26 September, holding the whole index shut, because the refusal named document-defects.csv as the remedy and no code read that file
evidence: manifest 65caf52de3b0…, disk a15a81c7d1ac…; superseded by state-dls/assessedvalues-2026-09-26-272171893ca3.xlsx, which carries its own sha256 in its name. Nothing is lost: the gate reports all documents this tree holds are in the bucket, read back and compared
